title: Terraform IaC Module Quality and Change Impact Analysis for Multi Environment Deployments Drift Detection and Safe Rollback
content: Terraform is widely used to manage cloud infrastructure through code. This method makes it easier to repeat setups and track changes. Still, large multi environment deployments face real problems. Complex modules increase the chance of mistakes. Risky changes can replace or delete critical resources. Drift creates differences between what the code says and what actually runs in the cloud. When failures occur, recovery may take too long. This study presents a framework that measures module complexity, calculates change risk before deployment, detects drift automatically, and restores the last stable state after failure. The experiment used 45 Terraform modules across Development, Staging, and Production environments. A total of 120 deployment scenarios were tested under both a standard workflow and the proposed framework. Performance was evaluated using Deployment Failure Rate (DFR), Drift Detection Accuracy (DDA), and Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR). The results show clear differences. Failure rates dropped from 18.3% to 6.7%. Drift detection accuracy rose from 61.2% to 93.5%. Recovery time decreased from 42.6 minutes to 18.4 minutes. Statistical analysis confirmed that these changes were significant. The evidence suggests that early risk calculation, continuous drift monitoring, and structured rollback improve the stability of Terraform deployments across multiple environments.
